Browse the [Shiny gallery](shiny-gallery.html) to open a standalone app, or
run the examples here alongside their R source. The first launch downloads R
and its dependencies. The apps use the highcharter version documented here.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(htmltools)
demo <- function(slug, title, height = 450) {
  src <- file.path("..", "pkgdown", "shiny", slug, "app.R")
  url <- paste0("../live/", slug, "/index.html")
  tagList(
    tags$details(
      ontoggle = "if (this.open) { const f = this.querySelector('iframe'); if (!f.hasAttribute('src')) f.src = f.dataset.src; }",
      tags$summary(paste("Run", title)),
      tags$iframe(
        title = title,
        `data-src` = url,
        width = "100%",
        height = height,
        style = "border:0"
      )
    ),
    tags$details(
      tags$summary("R source"),
      tags$pre(tags$code(paste(readLines(src), collapse = "\n")))
    ),
    tags$p(tags$a(
      href = url,
      "Open the app in its own tab",
      target = "_blank",
      rel = "noopener"
    ))
  )
}
```

## Basics

Select **Sepal** or **Petal**. The same 150 flowers move to their new coordinates.
Put `highchartOutput("flowers")` in the UI and read `input$measure` inside
`renderHighchart()` to rebuild the plot when the measurement changes.

```{r basic, echo=FALSE}
demo("basic", "the iris explorer")
```

## Proxies

Start with twelve months of air passenger counts. **Add a month** appends one
observation with `hcpxy_add_point()`. **Columns** changes the series type with
`hcpxy_update_series()`. Switch back to **Line** and your added months are
still there. Both controls target the series ID `traffic` through
`highchartProxy("passengers", session)`.

```{r proxy, echo=FALSE}
demo("proxy", "the passenger chart")
```

For an example that replaces a whole Stock series and sets the visible date
range, [run the Stock proxy app](../live/stock/index.html) or
[read the Stock walkthrough](stock.html#update-a-series-and-its-visible-range-in-shiny).

## Events

Click a band in the equalizer. Shiny receives its ID at
`input$eq_point_click$pointid` automatically. Drag the band and release it.
The app uses only `hc_add_event_point(event = "drop")` to send the final gain
in decibels to `input$eq_point_drop$y`.

```{r events, echo=FALSE}
demo("events", "the equalizer", height = 490)
```

The output ID, scope and case-sensitive Highcharts event name determine the
input. For example, `hc_add_event_series(event = "mouseOver")` would send
the hovered series to `input$eq_series_mouseOver`.

## Linked views

Click a species in the overview to see the individual flowers in the detail
chart. The server reads `input$overview_point_click$pointid` and uses a proxy
to replace the detail series and its title. This combines the two preceding
patterns and keeps both charts mounted.

```{r linked, echo=FALSE}
demo("linked", "the linked charts", height = 430)
```

To run an example from a local checkout, load the package and open the app directory:

```{r local-app, eval=FALSE}
pkgload::load_all()
shiny::runApp("pkgdown/shiny/events")
```

The [original Shiny examples](https://github.com/jbkunst/highcharter-shiny)
include the full [proxy playground](https://github.com/jbkunst/highcharter-shiny/tree/master/02-proxy-functions)
and a [population explorer with linked views](https://github.com/jbkunst/highcharter-shiny/tree/master/08-idb-viz).
